title: Out West
subtitle: Viaggio verso ovest
intro: Ten days in August: a flight to Calgary delayed by storms, lost luggage, Banff and Lake Louise, a black bear at a safe distance, a hotel that had been overbooked, Vancouver's rain. Announcements, apologies, compensation forms. Sofia's photos; Chiara's complaint email, now perfect. This unit builds the English [[passive]] in all tenses, [[get + past participle]], travel phrasal verbs, and the articles-with-geographic-names map.
objectives: Usare il passivo in tutti i tempi: [[the flight has been delayed]], [[the bags were lost]], [[your room will be upgraded]]
Usare get + participio come passivo informale: [[I got lost]], [[we got paid late]], [[they got refunded]]
Capire e produrre annunci e notizie: [[your attention please, flight 221 has been cancelled]]
Usare i phrasal verb del viaggio: [[check in / out, take off, set off, pick up, get in / on / off, put up with, look forward to]]
Scegliere l'articolo giusto con i nomi geografici: [[the Rockies]], [[Lake Louise]], [[Canada]], [[the UK]], [[the Pacific]]
canDo: B1 · Spoken production: can describe experiences and natural settings in detail.
B1 · Spoken interaction: can handle travel problems and file complaints with the right register.
B1 · Reading: can read airport and train announcements and basic news reports.
B1 · Writing: can write a travel complaint email or a short review.
B1 · Listening: can follow announcements and news in a formal passive register.

sections.title: The 401 to Pearson, then west
sections.intro: The three scenes of a trip: a Pearson delay with a cancelled flight; a hotel in Banff that had been overbooked; a day in Vancouver's rain. Listen for the passive (has been delayed, had been overbooked, is cleaned), get + participle (got lost, got refunded), and the small formal English of announcements.

blocks.title: Pearson · Flight 221 · delays
blocks.setting: August 2, 7:40 p.m., Toronto Pearson, Terminal 1, Gate D54. Chiara and Sofia at the gate; the plane to Calgary should have left an hour ago. The gate agent is reading an announcement in the Air Canada tone. The screen reads: FLIGHT AC221 YYZ-YYC — DELAYED.

lines.t: Your attention please. Air Canada flight 221 to Calgary has been delayed due to thunderstorms over the Prairies. The new departure time is 21:40. We apologise for the inconvenience. Passengers are being offered a 10-dollar meal voucher at the information desk, which can be redeemed at any Terminal 1 restaurant.
lines.n: Attenzione, prego. Il volo Air Canada 221 per Calgary è stato ritardato per temporali sulle Praterie. Il nuovo orario di partenza è alle 21:40. Ci scusiamo per il disagio. Ai passeggeri viene offerto un voucher pasto da 10 dollari al banco informazioni, utilizzabile in qualsiasi ristorante del Terminal 1.
lines.note: Four passive constructions in one announcement: has been delayed, are being offered, can be redeemed. The register of airport English.

lines.t: Two hours. Great. — The voucher won't buy much at Pearson. Ten dollars gets you a sandwich without the drink. — At least they're giving us something. Last time I flew out of Rome, we got nothing.
lines.n: Due ore. Grande. — Il voucher non prende molto a Pearson. Dieci dollari ti compra un panino senza bevanda. — Almeno ci stanno dando qualcosa. L'ultima volta che sono volata da Roma, non ci hanno dato niente.
lines.note: Won't buy much: future negative. Ten dollars gets you a sandwich: present simple generic. We got nothing: past simple + get + object = received.

lines.t: You're set up for Rockies trips, Chiara. Your bag has been checked through to Calgary, I hope. Mine's been checked through to Vancouver — I'm getting off there, remember? — Mine's been checked all the way to Vancouver too; I switched the ticket last week.
lines.n: Sei preparata per il viaggio nelle Montagne Rocciose, Chiara. La tua valigia è stata registrata direttamente per Calgary, spero. La mia è stata registrata per Vancouver — scendo lì, ti ricordi? — Anche la mia è stata registrata per Vancouver; ho cambiato il biglietto la settimana scorsa.
lines.note: Has been checked through: present perfect passive. The passive is what you say when you don't know or don't care who did it (the airline, the system, somebody).

lines.t: Attention please. Flight 221 to Calgary is now boarding at Gate D54. Passengers in Zone 1 are invited to the gate first. Please have your boarding pass ready. Priority access passengers will be invited to board separately.
lines.n: Attenzione, prego. Il volo 221 per Calgary è in imbarco al gate D54. I passeggeri della Zona 1 sono invitati per primi al gate. Preparate la carta d'imbarco. I passeggeri con accesso prioritario saranno invitati a bordo separatamente.
lines.note: Is now boarding: present continuous. Are invited / will be invited: passive. Priority access, Zone 1: airline language.

lines.t: Look. The Rockies next week. I've been looking forward to this since February. — So have I. — If my bag gets lost at Calgary, I'll kill someone. — If your bag gets lost at Calgary, we'll go without you for a day and then come back for you.
lines.n: Guarda. Le Rocciose la prossima settimana. Lo aspetto da febbraio. — Anch'io. — Se la mia valigia si perde a Calgary, uccido qualcuno. — Se la tua valigia si perde a Calgary, andiamo senza di te per un giorno e poi torniamo a prenderti.
lines.note: I've been looking forward to this: present perfect continuous of look forward to. If my bag gets lost = passive with get. The casual version.

notes.phrase: has been delayed · are being offered · can be redeemed · has been checked through · is being boarded · will be invited
notes.note: Six passive constructions in one short airport scene. The passive is the music of announcements: 'something happens', agent omitted.

notes.phrase: get lost · get paid · got refunded · got nothing (= received nothing) · get off the plane
notes.note: The informal get + participle (passive) and get + object (receive).

notes.phrase: Pearson · YYZ (Toronto) · YYC (Calgary) · YVR (Vancouver) · the Prairies · the Rockies · boarding pass · gate agent · priority access · Zone 1
notes.note: The vocabulary of a Canadian airport.

blocks.title: Banff · the overbooked hotel
blocks.setting: August 3, 11:40 p.m., Banff, Alberta, elevation 1,383 m. The Elkhorn Lodge reception. The desk clerk's name tag reads BEN. Chiara, exhausted, with her bag and her booking.
blocks.register: formal between tourist and hotel clerk, with the small apology of a national park town

lines.t: Hi. Chiara Russo, I have a booking for tonight. — Hi. One moment. — Yes. I see your booking. Unfortunately, the room you were booked into has been given to another guest. The system overbooked us by two tonight; I'm so sorry.
lines.n: Salve. Chiara Russo, ho una prenotazione per stasera. — Salve. Un momento. — Sì, vedo la prenotazione. Purtroppo la camera che le avevamo assegnato è stata data a un altro ospite. Il sistema ha overprenotato di due stasera; mi dispiace davvero.
lines.note: You were booked into: past passive. Has been given: present perfect passive. The hotel's overbooking is a chronic problem in Banff in high season.

lines.t: Here's what I can offer. We're being told to put overbooked guests up at the Royal Canadian Lodge, which is seven minutes' walk from here, same price, same tier. A free dinner has been added to your stay there, and your parking has been waived. A shuttle van is being driven over right now if you'd like a ride.
lines.n: Ecco cosa le posso offrire. Ci stanno dicendo di sistemare gli ospiti overprenotati al Royal Canadian Lodge, a sette minuti a piedi da qui, stesso prezzo, stessa categoria. Una cena gratis le è stata aggiunta al soggiorno lì, e il parcheggio è stato rimborsato. Una navetta sta arrivando adesso se vuole un passaggio.
lines.note: Six passive sentences in a row. The register of a hotel making up for an overbooking. We're being told, a free dinner has been added, your parking has been waived, a shuttle van is being driven. The classic apology script.

lines.t: Thanks. I'll take the shuttle. Will my second night be upgraded? I was booked for three nights. — The second and third nights will be back here, in your original room category, with a free breakfast on both days. You've been downgraded tonight only, and compensated.
lines.n: Grazie. Prendo la navetta. La seconda notte sarà upgradata? Ero prenotata per tre notti. — La seconda e la terza notte saranno qui, nella categoria originale, con colazione gratis in entrambi i giorni. È stata downgradata solo stasera, e compensata.
lines.note: Will my second night be upgraded?: future passive question. The second and third nights will be back here: future passive. You've been downgraded… and compensated: present perfect passive.

lines.t: I'd like a written confirmation of all of this, for my records. Also, I need a receipt that shows the overbooking cost was absorbed by you, not me. If I had to pay anything extra, I'll want it refunded.
lines.n: Vorrei una conferma scritta di tutto, per i miei archivi. Inoltre mi serve una ricevuta che mostri che il costo dell'overbooking è stato assorbito da voi, non da me. Se dovessi pagare qualcosa in più, voglio il rimborso.
lines.note: Was absorbed by you: past passive with by + agent (the rare case when the agent matters). I'll want it refunded: future + want + object + past participle = the «want something done» pattern.

lines.t: Of course. Here's the printed confirmation and a receipt, both signed by me and stamped by the hotel. If anything else goes wrong, call me at this extension. I've been running this desk for eight years and this hasn't happened in two.
lines.n: Certo. Ecco la conferma stampata e la ricevuta, entrambe firmate da me e timbrate dall'hotel. Se qualcos'altro va storto, mi chiami a questo interno. Gestisco questo banco da otto anni e non è mai successo da due.
lines.note: Both signed by me and stamped by the hotel: past participles as adjectives (not full passive, but the shortened form). I've been running this desk for eight years: present perfect continuous.

notes.phrase: the room you were booked into · has been given · has been added · has been waived · is being driven · will be upgraded · will be back · have been downgraded · was absorbed by you
notes.note: Nine passive constructions in one hotel scene. The register of a Canadian apology.

blocks.title: Vancouver · the rain and the ferries
blocks.setting: August 7, 2 p.m., Granville Island public market, Vancouver. Steady drizzle, 17°C. Sofia and Chiara with ice cream from the Island Creamery, deciding whether to take a seabus or walk back to Yaletown. The Rockies are three days behind them.
blocks.register: casual between friends on a trip

lines.t: I got soaked. Just my shoulders — my jacket's waterproof. Vancouver rain is different: it's just here. In Toronto you get rained on; here you get rained in.
lines.n: Mi sono inzuppata. Solo le spalle — la giacca è impermeabile. La pioggia di Vancouver è diversa: è lì e basta. A Toronto ti arriva addosso; qui ti circonda.
lines.note: I got soaked: get + past participle = passive informal. You get rained on: get + passive participle, standard.

lines.t: I didn't bring enough warm stuff. If I had been better organised, I would've been warm now. — If I hadn't been dragged to the summit of Sulphur Mountain in a tank top yesterday, I wouldn't have caught a cold today.
lines.n: Non ho portato abbastanza roba calda. Se fossi stata più organizzata, sarei stata al caldo adesso. — Se non fossi stata trascinata in cima al Sulphur Mountain in canotta ieri, non avrei preso freddo oggi.
lines.note: If I hadn't been dragged… I wouldn't have caught: third conditional with the passive in the if-clause (had been dragged). Mixed with the second conditional in the first sentence.

lines.t: What's the plan for the afternoon? — The ferry to Victoria has been cancelled because of the swells. We can walk the sea wall at Stanley Park if the rain lets up. Or we can give up and go to a café. — Let's see what happens in half an hour.
lines.n: Che facciamo nel pomeriggio? — Il traghetto per Victoria è stato cancellato per il mare mosso. Possiamo camminare lungo il sea wall a Stanley Park se la pioggia smette. Oppure ci arrendiamo e andiamo in un caffè. — Vediamo in mezz'ora.
lines.note: The ferry has been cancelled: present perfect passive. The passive is used for announcements the news repeats and for impersonal responsibility.

lines.t: I love the Pacific. The Rockies are the Rockies, but the Pacific is wider. If you grew up on the Adriatic like you did, the Pacific is a different scale of thing.
lines.n: Amo il Pacifico. Le Rocciose sono le Rocciose, ma il Pacifico è più ampio. Se sei cresciuta sull'Adriatico come te, il Pacifico è un'altra scala di cosa.
lines.note: The Rockies, the Pacific: definite article with plural mountain ranges and oceans. The Adriatic: article with named sea.

lines.t: Four days ago I saw a black bear in Banff. Today I'm looking at the Pacific. Tomorrow I'll be back in Yaletown with a cold. Then home. — This is why we travel.
lines.n: Quattro giorni fa ho visto un orso nero a Banff. Oggi guardo il Pacifico. Domani sarò a Yaletown con un raffreddore. Poi a casa. — Ecco perché si viaggia.

notes.phrase: I got soaked · you get rained on · the ferry has been cancelled · if I hadn't been dragged · the Rockies · the Pacific · the Adriatic · Lake Louise · Banff · Sulphur Mountain
notes.note: A mix of informal passive (got + part.), formal passive (has been cancelled), and the articles with geographic names.

questions.q: «Our flight has been delayed» is in the:
questions.why: Has been + past participle = present perfect passive. The announcement voice.

questions.q: «I got soaked» means «I became soaked» (informal passive).
questions.why: Get + past participle is the colloquial passive. I got soaked, I got lost, I got paid.

questions.q: The flight ___ (delay, pres. perf. pass.). The room ___ (give, pres. perf. pass.) to another guest. Our bags ___ (lose, past simple pass.) at Calgary.
questions.n: Il volo è stato ritardato. La camera è stata data a un altro ospite. I nostri bagagli sono stati persi a Calgary.

sections.title: Flights, mountains, bears, Canada
sections.intro: Four themes: air travel, mountains and nature, animals and safety, and complaints and insurance.

ex.t: Flight 221 to Calgary has been delayed.
ex.n: Il volo 221 per Calgary è stato ritardato.

items.note: Flight number + letters + numbers. Direct flight / connecting flight. Red-eye: overnight flight.

ex.t: Please have your boarding pass ready.
ex.n: Preparate la carta d'imbarco.

items.note: Printed or on your phone (mobile boarding pass).

ex.t: The gate has changed from D54 to D22.
ex.n: Il gate è cambiato dal D54 al D22.

items.note: Gate change: cambio di gate. Boarding at Gate D22.

ex.t: The plane took off at 9:40 and landed in Calgary at midnight.
ex.n: L'aereo è decollato alle 9:40 ed è atterrato a Calgary a mezzanotte.

items.note: Takeoff and landing: nouns derived from the verbs.

ex.t: Online check-in opens 24 hours before.
ex.n: Il check-in online apre 24 ore prima.

items.note: Check in a bag: imbarcare un bagaglio. Check out of a hotel: lasciare l'hotel. Noun: a check-in.

ex.t: A three-hour layover in Toronto.
ex.n: Uno scalo di tre ore a Toronto.

items.note: Also stopover (slightly longer). Direct flight has no layover.

ex.t: Baggage claim is downstairs.
ex.n: Il ritiro bagagli è al piano di sotto.

items.note: Both uncountable. Carry-on: bagaglio a mano. Checked bag: bagaglio in stiva.

ex.t: A two-hour delay and a possible cancellation.
ex.n: Un ritardo di due ore e una possibile cancellazione.

items.note: The 2019 Air Passenger Protection Regulations guarantee compensation for both.

ex.t: The hotel was overbooked by two tonight.
ex.n: L'hotel ha overprenotato di due stasera.

items.note: Not «overbooking» as verb; use the passive. Chronic in Canadian national parks in July–August.

ex.t: I'm entitled to compensation for the overbooking.
ex.n: Ho diritto a un risarcimento per l'overbooking.

items.note: Compensation claim: richiesta di risarcimento. Entitled to: con il diritto a.

ex.t: A 10-dollar meal voucher at any Terminal 1 restaurant.
ex.n: Un buono pasto di 10 dollari in qualsiasi ristorante del Terminal 1.

items.note: Voucher: standard English. Also credit (digital).

ex.t: The Rockies are shared between Alberta and British Columbia.
ex.n: Le Rocciose sono condivise fra Alberta e British Columbia.

items.note: Also the Rocky Mountains. Mountain ranges take the (plural). Also the Alps, the Pyrenees, the Himalayas.

ex.t: The peak of Mount Robson is 3,954 metres.
ex.n: La cima del Monte Robson è a 3.954 metri.

items.note: Summit = topmost point; peak = pointed top. Mount + name (singular mountain).

ex.t: Lake Louise is in a valley.
ex.n: Lake Louise è in una valle.

items.note: The Fraser Valley, the Okanagan Valley. Valleys in Canada are often enormous.

ex.t: Lake Louise, Lake Moraine, Lake Minnewanka — the glacier lakes.
ex.n: Lake Louise, Moraine, Minnewanka — i laghi glaciali.

items.note: Lake + name (Lake Louise, no article in English). Compare: il lago di Garda. In French Canada: le lac + name.

ex.t: The Columbia Icefield is one of the largest glaciers in the Rockies.
ex.n: Il Columbia Icefield è uno dei ghiacciai più grandi delle Rocciose.

items.note: Ice field: a complex of glaciers. Both are in retreat.

ex.t: Takakkaw Falls is one of Canada's tallest waterfalls.
ex.n: Le Takakkaw Falls sono fra le cascate più alte del Canada.

items.note: Also simply falls (plural, like Niagara Falls). Verb: to fall.

ex.t: The Johnston Canyon trail is 2.4 km one way.
ex.n: Il sentiero del Johnston Canyon è di 2,4 km solo andata.

items.note: Hiking trail / bike trail / ski trail. Trailhead: il punto d'inizio.

ex.t: We hiked for three hours. We went hiking at Lake Louise.
ex.n: Abbiamo camminato per tre ore. Siamo andati in escursione a Lake Louise.

items.note: Hike as verb and noun. A long hike: una lunga escursione.

ex.t: Tunnel Mountain campground books up months in advance.
ex.n: Il campeggio Tunnel Mountain si prenota mesi prima.

items.note: RV camping: con camper. Tent camping: in tenda. Book up: esaurirsi.

ex.t: Keep 100 metres from large wildlife.
ex.n: Mantieni 100 metri dalla fauna di taglia grande.

items.note: Uncountable. Also the Wildlife Act, specific to each province.

ex.t: We saw a black bear from a safe distance.
ex.n: Abbiamo visto un orso nero da una distanza sicura.

items.note: Black bear (common, smaller) vs grizzly bear (big, dangerous). Polar bear: orso polare.

ex.t: Elk cross the road in Banff; moose stop traffic.
ex.n: I wapiti attraversano la strada a Banff; gli alci fermano il traffico.

items.note: Elk (plural elk, 300+ kg): un wapiti. Moose (plural moose, 500+ kg): un alce. Easy to confuse.

ex.t: I spotted a bear in a berry patch.
ex.n: Ho avvistato un orso fra i mirtilli.

items.note: Noun: un avvistamento (sighting). Also bird-spotting = birdwatching.

ex.t: Keep a safe distance of 100 metres from bears.
ex.n: Mantieni una distanza sicura di 100 metri dagli orsi.

items.note: Safe distance, long distance, within walking distance. Parks Canada signage uses metres.

ex.t: Carry bear spray on long trails.
ex.n: Porta lo spray antiorso sui sentieri lunghi.

items.note: Legal in Canada; sold at MEC. Different from pepper spray in strength.

ex.t: Park at the trailhead and follow the signs.
ex.n: Parcheggia all'inizio del sentiero e segui i cartelli.

items.note: The marked starting point of a trail, with maps and warnings.

ex.t: There was a bear warning posted at the trailhead.
ex.n: C'era un avviso per gli orsi all'inizio del sentiero.

items.note: To issue a warning. Red / yellow / green warning levels at Parks Canada.

ex.t: Feeding wildlife carries a 25,000-dollar fine.
ex.n: Dare cibo alla fauna comporta una multa di 25.000 dollari.

items.note: Fine as noun = multa. Fine as adjective = bene / di qualità.

ex.t: File a lost luggage report at the baggage office.
ex.n: Fai un reclamo per bagaglio smarrito all'ufficio bagagli.

items.note: Standard airline form. File a claim: presentare una richiesta.

ex.t: A police report for stolen items.
ex.n: Un verbale della polizia per gli oggetti rubati.

items.note: File a report. Also report = segnalare (verb).

ex.t: Travel insurance covers delays, cancellations and medical.
ex.n: L'assicurazione di viaggio copre ritardi, cancellazioni e medico.

items.note: A travel insurance policy. Deductible: franchigia.

ex.t: File a claim with the airline within 30 days.
ex.n: Presenta la richiesta alla compagnia entro 30 giorni.

items.note: File a claim, submit a claim. Insurance claim: denuncia all'assicurazione.

ex.t: A refund of the ticket price minus taxes.
ex.n: Un rimborso del prezzo del biglietto meno le tasse.

items.note: Verb: to refund. Also reimburse (longer, more formal).

ex.t: You are entitled to compensation for a delay over three hours.
ex.n: Hai diritto a un risarcimento per un ritardo superiore a tre ore.

items.note: Entitled to + noun / to + inf. Also «within your rights».

ex.t: I had to put up with the delay for five hours.
ex.n: Ho dovuto sopportare il ritardo per cinque ore.

items.note: Inseparable. Also tolerate, endure (more formal).

ex.t: I'm looking forward to the Rockies.
ex.n: Non vedo l'ora delle Rocciose.

items.note: Followed by -ing or noun. Not followed by to + inf.: look forward to going (not look forward to go).

ex.t: We set off at 5 a.m. for the trailhead.
ex.n: Siamo partiti alle 5 per l'inizio del sentiero.

items.note: Set off is more common for a trip; set out can also mean to begin.

ex.t: If the rain doesn't let up, we'll give up and go to a café.
ex.n: Se la pioggia non smette, ci arrendiamo e andiamo in un caffè.

items.note: Separable (give it up). Let up: diminuire (said of rain, pain, pressure).

sections.title: Passive, get-passive, geographic articles
sections.intro: Three pieces: the English passive in all tenses, get + past participle for the informal passive, and the article rules with geographic names.

blocks.title: The passive voice
blocks.rule: The English passive turns the object of an active sentence into the subject of a passive one. The agent is dropped (because unknown, unimportant, or obvious) or added with by + agent. Form: be (in the right tense) + past participle. Active: Air Canada delayed the flight. Passive: The flight was delayed (by Air Canada). The passive exists in every tense: present simple (is checked), present cont. (is being checked), past simple (was checked), past cont. (was being checked), present perfect (has been checked), past perfect (had been checked), future (will be checked), future perfect (will have been checked), modal (can be / must be / might be + checked). The passive dominates: airline announcements, hotel apologies, news reports, scientific writing, instructions. Transitive verbs only. Intransitive verbs (go, come, arrive, happen, die) have no passive. Verbs with two objects (give, send, offer, tell) can be passivised two ways: Priya was given a visa / A visa was given to Priya.

blocks.caption: The passive across tenses
head: Tense
Active
Passive
rows: They will have checked the bag.
The bag will have been checked.

items.t: The flight has been delayed. The baggage is being loaded. Passengers are invited to board. A meal voucher has been added to every booking.
items.n: Il volo è stato ritardato. I bagagli vengono caricati. I passeggeri sono invitati a bordo. Un buono pasto è stato aggiunto a ogni prenotazione.

items.t: The ferry has been cancelled due to high swells. A new sailing has not yet been scheduled.
items.n: Il traghetto è stato cancellato per il mare mosso. Un nuovo imbarco non è ancora stato programmato.

items.t: Our bags were lost at Calgary and have been found at Vancouver three days later.
items.n: I nostri bagagli sono stati persi a Calgary e sono stati trovati a Vancouver tre giorni dopo.

blocks.title: Il passivo italiano
blocks.text: Italian passive: essere + participio (il volo è stato ritardato). Or venire + participio (il volo viene ritardato — only for processes, not states, more journalistic). Or andare + participio for obligation (va compilato = must be filled in). English uses only be + part. Italian also has si-passivante (si vendono biciclette = bikes are sold) which English doesn't. Agent in both: by + agent (inglese) · da + agente (italiano).

items.right: The flight is delayed. (passive) OR The flight delays [its departure]. (not idiomatic)

items.wrong: She was happened to be here.

items.right: The letter was written yesterday. OR The letter has been written. (today, with present perfect)
items.why: Match the tense: past time → past passive.

items.right: A gift was given to me. / I was given a gift.
items.why: Two passives for a dative-direct-object verb. English prefers I was given…

blocks.title: Get + past participle
blocks.rule: The informal / colloquial passive. Get + past participle = (become) + participle: I got lost (mi sono perso), we got paid late (siamo stati pagati in ritardo), they got refunded (sono stati rimborsati). The agent is almost never named. Get-passive differs from be-passive in two ways: it is more informal (speech / casual writing); it implies change or action (the person did something or something happened to them). Compare: the bag was checked (status) vs the bag got checked (process). Common collocations: get lost / get married / get engaged / get divorced / get hurt / get injured / get paid / get fired / get hired / get caught / get stuck / get stolen / get soaked / get drunk. In formal English, use the be-passive; in speech, the get-passive is everywhere.

blocks.caption: Get-passive vs be-passive
head: Pattern
Example
rows: I got lost in Vancouver. We got paid on Friday.
The car got stuck in the mud.
I got the furnace fixed. She got her hair cut.

items.t: I got soaked in Vancouver. Sofia got sick in Banff. We got charged for a room upgrade we didn't want.
items.n: Mi sono inzuppata a Vancouver. Sofia si è ammalata a Banff. Ci hanno addebitato un upgrade che non volevamo.

items.t: If my bag gets lost at Calgary, I'll kill someone. — If your bag gets lost at Calgary, we'll come back for you.
items.n: Se la mia valigia si perde a Calgary, uccido qualcuno. — Se la tua si perde, torniamo a prenderti.

items.t: Chiara's parents got married in 1991. Priya got hired by the bakery in 2023.
items.n: I genitori di Chiara si sono sposati nel 1991. Priya è stata assunta dalla pasticceria nel 2023.

items.wrong: I got losing. I got loss.
items.why: Get + past participle, not -ing or noun.
Get + past participle, not get + to + inf. (that's a different idiom: got to = had to, informal).

blocks.title: Articles with geographic names
blocks.rule: English uses the with some geographic names and no article with others. The rules in short. The with: plural mountain ranges (the Rockies, the Alps, the Himalayas), oceans and seas (the Pacific, the Atlantic, the Mediterranean, the North Sea), rivers (the Thames, the Nile, the Fraser), deserts (the Sahara, the Gobi), island groups (the Bahamas, the Philippines, the British Isles), gulfs (the Gulf of Mexico), named points of the compass (the North, the South, the West), hotel / cinema / theatre / newspaper names (the Elkhorn, the Globe, the Times), many political entities (the United States, the UK, the Netherlands, the Czech Republic, the European Union). No article with: single mountains (Mount Robson, Mount Fuji, Everest), single lakes (Lake Louise, Lake Ontario, Lake Como), single islands (Vancouver Island, Sicily), continents (North America, Europe, Asia), most countries (Canada, Italy, France, Japan), cities (Toronto, Rome), streets (Yonge Street, Via del Corso — unless given with the article: on the Danforth), parks (Banff National Park, Hyde Park). The exceptions pile up (the Hague, the Vatican) and are learned case-by-case.

Second (glottal t): [[The mountain is important. Button up your coat. Manhattan is cold.]] Four glottal t's. Third (news passive): [[The ferry has been cancelled. A compensation plan has been announced. Services will be restored by Monday.]]

items.q: Write a six-sentence account of a travel problem, using at least three passive constructions (one with the agent by + agent), one get-passive, one travel phrasal verb (take off, set off, check in, pick up, put up with, look forward to), and one geographic name with the correct article (the Rockies, Lake Louise, Mount Robson, the Pacific, the Netherlands, Canada).
items.model: Last August my flight to Calgary was delayed by Air Canada due to thunderstorms over the Prairies. The boarding was finally called at 10 p.m., three hours late. My bag got lost in the connection and was found two days later at Vancouver, and in the meantime I had to put up with wearing the same T-shirt in Banff. The hotel at the Elkhorn Lodge had been overbooked, and I was moved to the Royal Canadian Lodge, where a free dinner had been added to the stay. The Rockies made up for all of it: Lake Louise at sunrise is a different scale of thing. I'd been looking forward to it since February, and even with the delay, it was worth every hour.
items.hint: Last August my flight was… · The boarding was called… · My bag got lost… · The hotel had been overbooked… · The Rockies made up for… · I'd been looking forward…

sections.title: The country that goes on, bears, airports
sections.intro: Three pages: Canada's six time zones and distances; Parks Canada and bear country; Air Canada vs WestJet and the Air Passenger Protection Regulations.

blocks.text: Six time zones and the empty middle

Canada is the second-largest country in the world by area, with [[six time zones]] (Pacific, Mountain, Central, Eastern, Atlantic and Newfoundland — the last offset by 30 minutes, not 60). Toronto to Vancouver is 4,400 km by road, 4 hours by flight, 4 days by Via Rail (the Canadian), 23 days by bike. Between Winnipeg (Manitoba) and Vancouver, the Trans-Canada Highway crosses 1,800 km of prairie and 500 km of mountains with roughly 60 cities and dozens of First Nations communities in between. Flying is the main option for east-west travel: [[Air Canada]] and [[WestJet]] are the two main carriers; [[Porter Airlines]] runs regional and growing transcon flights; [[Flair]] and [[Lynx]] are the budget options. In practice, cross-country travel takes serious time and money, and most Canadians know their province, their neighbouring provinces, and the two or three big cities they visit. Chiara's trip is more than she usually does — many Toronto residents have never been west of Winnipeg.

[[Parks Canada]] runs 48 national parks and 171 national historic sites, with a budget of around 1 billion CAD. The big western parks are [[Banff]] (established 1885, the oldest), [[Jasper]], [[Yoho]], [[Kootenay]] (collectively a UNESCO World Heritage site), [[Waterton Lakes]], and in BC [[Pacific Rim]] and [[Mount Robson]]. Entry is 10–20 CAD a day or 75 CAD for the yearly Discovery Pass. The bear rules: keep [[100 metres]] from any bear, 30 metres from elk / moose; carry [[bear spray]] on backcountry trails; store food in bear bins or your car's trunk; make noise while hiking (talk, clap); never feed wildlife (25,000 CAD fine). About 2% of Banff's 4 million annual visitors see a bear, usually from a car on the Bow Valley Parkway. Grizzlies (around 60 in Banff) and black bears (around 100) coexist. The park service closes trails and campgrounds when a bear is active in an area; respect the closures. Chiara saw a black bear on the Johnston Canyon trail from 80 metres, exactly where you want to see one.

blocks.title: The Air Passenger Protection Regulations
blocks.text: Canada's [[APPR]], in force since 2019, gives passengers specific rights for flight disruption. The three categories: (1) events within the airline's control (e.g. staffing, routine maintenance): the airline must offer rebooking + 400 to 1,000 CAD compensation after 3 hours delay, more for a cancellation. (2) Events within control but required for safety (e.g. a mechanical issue found at the gate): rebooking + reasonable care (meals, hotel), but no cash compensation. (3) Events outside the airline's control (weather, air traffic, security): rebooking + reasonable care, no compensation. Lost baggage: 2,350 CAD maximum. Delayed baggage: reasonable expenses for the first 21 days. Denied boarding (bump): 900–2,400 CAD. The claim process goes through the airline first, then the [[Canadian Transportation Agency]]. Chiara's delay was a category 3 (thunderstorms), so Air Canada owed her reasonable care (which they gave: 10-dollar voucher), not cash.

[[Vancouver]], population 710,000 (metro 2.6 million), BC's biggest city, sits where the North Shore mountains meet the Strait of Georgia. Founded in 1886 by the Canadian Pacific Railway. The three essentials: [[Stanley Park]] (a 400-hectare forest right next to downtown, with a 10-km sea wall for walking and cycling); [[Granville Island]] (a public market and arts complex under the Granville Bridge); [[the North Shore]] (Grouse Mountain, Lynn Canyon, Capilano Suspension Bridge). The climate is Pacific Northwest: mild (average January 4°C, July 18°C) and wet (300 mm of rain in November alone). Housing is expensive (average single-family home: 1.8 million CAD in 2026). It is Canada's most Asian city: 50% of residents identify as Asian; the largest ethnic groups are Chinese (28%), South Asian (12%) and Filipino (6%). From Vancouver's seawall, the Pacific stretches to Russia and Japan. For an Italian who grew up on the Adriatic (max 1,500 km across), this is a reorientation of scale.

groups.title: The passive
rows: form: be + past participle, in every tense
is checked, is being checked, was checked, has been checked, had been checked, will be checked
uses: announcements, news, instructions, scientific writing; agent omitted or with by
The flight has been delayed by Air Canada.
two-object verbs can be passivised two ways
A gift was given to me. / I was given a gift.
intransitive verbs have no passive (go, happen, arrive)

groups.title: Get-passive
rows: get + past participle = informal passive (speech, casual writing)
I got lost. We got paid. They got married.
dynamic / process sense: something happened, change of state
The bag got checked = the bag went through check-in.
common collocations: get lost / married / divorced / engaged / hurt / fired / hired / caught / stuck / paid / soaked / drunk
get something done (unit 17): I got the furnace fixed
